blocks.intro: Disposal work in McHenry depends on what your home drains into.

items.body: Most McHenry homes on city sewer can run a standard disposal without issue, as long as grease stays out.
In parts of McHenry County, homes drain to a septic tank. A disposal adds food solids to the tank, so it may need pumping more often. Ask us about a septic-rated unit.
A 1990s or 2000s home may still have its first or second disposal. Most last about 8 to 15 years.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Can I have a garbage disposal with a septic system?
items.preview: Yes, but plan on more frequent tank pumping.
items.answer: Yes. A disposal adds solids to the tank, so it may need pumping more often. A septic-rated disposal helps break waste down. We can explain the options.

items.preview: Jams and loose connections are repairs. A leaking body or dead motor means replace.
items.answer: A jam, a tripped reset or a loose connection can be fixed. A leaking housing or burned-out motor means a new unit.

items.q: What shouldn't go down a disposal?
items.preview: Grease, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
items.answer: Grease and oil, bones, fibrous scraps like celery and corn husks, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
Many last around 8 to 15 years. Frequent jams, leaks and louder grinding mean it's near the end.

items.q: Why does my disposal smell even after cleaning?
items.preview: Food trapped under the splash guard or grease in the drain.
items.answer: Food trapped under the rubber splash guard and grease in the drain line are the usual causes. Run cold water after each use. If the smell keeps coming back, the line may need cleaning.

items.answer: It depends on the unit and whether plumbing or electrical changes are needed. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
